note: Physical-validation run plan (docs/Physical_validation.md, TASK-066, TASK-068 D9). Offsets only, in metres from the site reference; no coordinates. Built into one spec.json per arm by pv_plan.py, which refuses a plan whose kangaroo leaves the fence less the orbit radius; flown in SITL with `python3 -m kangaroo_follow.demo --stage --plan --arm <id>`.

point.note: Flown first and held once for 45 s (one 70 m orbit at 16 m/s takes 27.5 s), at the fence's deepest point (68 m spare), away from the shared start; the kangaroo then walks to the shared start at the plan speed (an unscored transit). One lap of each run and no rests (author, 2026-10-10): every run starts and ends at the shared start, so the runs chain directly; 914 s (15.2 min) per arm at 6 m/s (was 518 s at 11 m/s; kangaroo slowed to 6 m/s on 2026-10-11 after flight 44, where the 12.5 m/s kangaroo outran the Bixler), one battery per arm to be confirmed.

cs_sampling.note: Heap (2026-10-10): the guidance samples its CS approach path's straights every delta_d_m (0.5 m) only for the first fine_m metres of the path (the carrot is read 30 m along it; AH replans every tick) and every coarse_m after, so a far approach no longer costs about 1.25 kB per metre. Leaves the guidance unchanged (tests/unit/test_hardware_val_merged.py). Remove this block to sample the whole path, as the Python harness.

flight_card.note: Active only (HVAL_OUT 1), one arm across every run before the next arm. SCR_HEAP_SIZE 750000: the board's limit (author, 2026-10-10). Measured 2026-10-10 in SITL with both scripts and heap expansion disabled (SCR_DEBUG_OPTS 64): 0H, FH and AH each flew the whole plan at 750000 with no memory error; the heap in use between ticks was about 310 kB (median), and the highest reading before an emergency collection 730 kB. That needed spec.json without rand_legs (sdcard.py) and kangaroo_source.lua loading mavlink_msgs and sitl_adsb only when used; before those, every arm ran out of memory on engagement. Confirm on the board (SCR_DEBUG_OPTS 2) before flight.
